AZ-2026-SB1723.aiSummary: The new law changes the rules for domestic violence protection orders. It lets a court require the defendant to give the other person identifying details, like a home address, job place, or vehicle info, if there is reason to think physical harm may happen. It also adds rules about notice if a person who was given exclusive use of the home moves out, and it keeps and serves these orders through the court and law enforcement.

AZ-2026-HB2114.aiSummary: The law changes motorcycle registration rules and sets up a motorcycle safety fund. A motorcycle registration can be renewed only if at least one owner is licensed to ride in Arizona, with a 30-day temporary registration allowed for someone enrolled in approved training. The state must put $1 from each motorcycle registration fee into the fund, which can pay for motorcycle safety programs and some training scholarships. It was signed into law on June 22, 2026, and takes effect after December 31, 2026.

AZ-2026-SB1205.aiSummary: The law limits what cities and towns can do about wheel boots on private property and sets state rules for when booting is allowed. It requires signs at private lots, sets release rules, and says booting services must be able to release a vehicle 24 hours a day. It also sets booting fees at $90 to $150, allows some added fees in limited cases, and bars booting certain vehicles like marked emergency vehicles, tax-exempt plate vehicles, and cars with an occupant.

AZ-2026-SB1037.aiSummary: The measure would change voter registration checks, including when county recorders mail notices, mark a voter inactive, or cancel a registration after an address change. It would also require the secretary of state to keep Arizona in a multistate electronic voter registration system, and it would change rules for presidential preference election ballots and early voting. It would affect county recorders, election officials, and registered voters. The bill passed the Legislature but was vetoed by the governor.

AZ-2026-HB2793.aiSummary: The bill would change the rules for how cities and towns in Arizona annex, or add, nearby land. It sets steps for filing, notices, hearings, petitions, and public review, and it lets a city or town skip the waiting period and hearing if one property owner controls all the land to be annexed. It also changes some map, notice, and zoning rules for annexed land and was passed and signed by the governor.

AZ-2026-HB2380.aiSummary: School district governing boards would have to meet at the most convenient public place in the district when one is available, and could meet elsewhere if no such place is available. They could also approve salary or other expense orders between meetings if the board had already passed a resolution and later ratified the order. The bill also changes some school board powers tied to district money and other duties.

AZ-2026-HB2226.aiSummary: The law requires a court to ask a person at their first court appearance whether they are a veteran. If the court confirms veteran status, it must notify the prosecutor, and the person may be told about services from the state veterans agency and may be considered for veterans court or another treatment or diversion program in some cases. If veteran status is unclear, the prosecutor must let the person or their lawyer show proof, such as a DD-214 form, which is a discharge record from the military.

AZ-2026-HB2170.aiSummary: The bill would bar some China-based companies from bidding on or getting Arizona state contracts for electronic or information technology. Companies that seek these contracts would have to sign a letter saying they are not covered by the ban and are not buying from a banned company for resale. A false letter could bring a $100,000 fine, contract ending, and a 60-month ban on bidding for state contracts.

AZ-2026-HB2100.aiSummary: Counties would be allowed to set rules for small land subdivisions of 6 to 10 lots on land that is not subject to certain water supply rules, as long as each lot is at least 2 acres. A person applying for one would need to file a public report and make sure each lot has legal access. If a county adopts such a rule, it would have to give written notice to the state real estate department. The bill passed the legislature but was vetoed by the governor.

AZ-2026-HB2016.aiSummary: This law changes Arizona tax penalty rules for late or missing returns and other tax filing problems. It affects taxpayers and some businesses that file or pay state taxes, including people who miss deadlines, give wrong information, or fail to pay amounts owed. The law also sets or changes penalty amounts for some tobacco tax and cigarette label violations.
